claims.text: Frequency of friend networking site use has an indirect effect on adolescents' social self-esteem.
Frequency of friend networking site use has an indirect effect on adolescents' well-being.
Friend networking site use stimulates the number of relationships formed on the site.
Friend networking site use stimulates the frequency with which adolescents receive feedback on their profiles.
Positive feedback on profile enhances adolescents' social self-esteem.
Positive feedback on profile enhances adolescents' well-being.
Negative feedback on profile decreases adolescents' social self-esteem.
Negative feedback on profile decreases adolescents' well-being.

evidence.description: Structural equation modeling of survey data from 881 adolescents showed an indirect effect of site use frequency on social self-esteem.
Structural equation modeling of survey data from 881 adolescents showed an indirect effect of site use frequency on well-being.
Survey results indicated that use of the friend networking site stimulated the number of relationships formed on the site.
Survey results indicated that use of the friend networking site stimulated the frequency of profile feedback received.
Structural equation modeling showed positive feedback on profiles enhanced social self-esteem.
Structural equation modeling showed positive feedback on profiles enhanced well-being.
Structural equation modeling showed negative feedback decreased self-esteem.
Structural equation modeling showed negative feedback decreased well-being.

methodologies.name: Structural Equation Modeling of Survey Data
methodologies.description: Adolescents with online profiles on a Dutch friend networking site completed a survey, and structural equation modeling was used to evaluate indirect effects on self-esteem and well-being.
datasets: Survey of Dutch friend networking site users (N=881)
conditions: Had an online profile on a Dutch friend networking site
